features.name: argument_has_hedging_markers
features.definition: Does the OP's argument use modest or uncertain epistemic markers (e.g., hedges like 'maybe', 'I think', 'perhaps', 'might', 'it seems') in the OP's own assertions?
features.spec: Read only `argument`. Return 1 if the OP's own assertions contain at least one modest/uncertain epistemic marker (hedges, tentative modals such as might/may/could used epistemically, 'perhaps', 'maybe', 'I think/I suppose', 'seems', 'probably', explicit admissions of uncertainty). Return 0 if none. Ignore markers only inside quotations attributed to others and not adopted by the OP. Do not count OP view-change/delta-award announcements, edits reporting the outcome, or post-outcome updates as evidence. Empty argument gives 0; missing/malformed gives null.

features.name: argument_has_high_modality_assertions
features.definition: Does the OP's argument use high-modality, certain assertions (e.g., 'must', 'always', 'never', 'definitely', 'obviously') in the OP's own assertions?
features.spec: Read only `argument`. Return 1 if the OP's own assertions contain at least one high-modality/certainty marker (e.g., must, have to, always, never, certainly, definitely, undoubtedly, obviously, clearly, absolutely, 'there is no way', categorical claims stated with strong certainty). Return 0 if none. Ignore markers only inside quotations attributed to others and not adopted by the OP. Do not count OP view-change/delta-award announcements, edits reporting the outcome, or post-outcome updates as evidence. Empty argument gives 0; missing/malformed gives null.

h0: Discussions whose arguments contain hedging markers are no more likely to show view change than those with high-modality assertions (hedging effect minus high-modality effect on delta is zero or negative).
h1: Arguments with argument_has_hedging_markers are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than arguments with argument_has_high_modality_assertions.
note: The claim is a comparison of hedged versus high-modality arguments. In this formula, each coefficient is relative to a baseline with neither marker type (overlap and neither cases exist), so neither coefficient equals the hedging-minus-high-modality contrast; no single design-matrix column represents it, hence term=null. I did not construct a difference score. Both measurements are presence-based (no count/intensity scale assumed). Uses current argument text; the argument may contain edits or outcome announcements, so raw text is not pre-outcome; the prompt excludes outcome announcements as evidence of the markers. Associations only.
